stories.headline: Alibaba and China Telecom Launch AI Data Center With 10,000 Homegrown Zhenwu Chips

key_facts.fact: Alibaba and China Telecom launched a data center in Shaoguan, Guangdong province, powered by 10,000 of Alibaba's self-developed Zhenwu AI chips, designed for AI training and inferencing.
The cluster is designed to support training of AI models with hundreds of billions of parameters and is expected to expand to a scale of 100,000 chips.

The new cluster delivers a 30% improvement in training and inference efficiency, with individual card throughput up nearly tenfold versus previous-generation systems and end-to-end network latency held to 4 microseconds.

Alibaba's Zhenwu chips were developed by its T-Head semiconductor unit and the launch follows the activation last month of a Huawei Ascend 910C-based computing cluster, both responding to U.S. export restrictions on Nvidia AI chips.

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu announced creation of a new technology committee to 'accelerate' the company's AI development, which he will head alongside Chief AI Architect Zhou Jingren, Alibaba Cloud CTO Li Feifei, and Alibaba Group CTO Wu Zeming.
Alibaba's stock rose nearly 8% on the data center news as Beijing intensifies its push for self-sufficient AI infrastructure under its 15th five-year plan.

stories.headline: The Information: Alibaba Is the Maker of HappyHorse, the Anonymous Video Model Topping Leaderboards

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on April 8, 2026 that Alibaba Group anonymously released a new AI video generation model called HappyHorse-1.0, which has risen to the top of Artificial Analysis' AI video model leaderboard, above ByteDance's Seedance 2.0.

On Artificial Analysis' blind-tested Video Arena, HappyHorse-1.0 took #1 in both text-to-video (no audio) with an Elo of 1333 and image-to-video (no audio) with an Elo of 1392, ahead of Dreamina Seedance 2.0 at 1273.

Technically, HappyHorse-1.0 is described as a 15-billion-parameter, 40-layer single-stream self-attention transformer that ingests text, image, video and audio tokens into one unified sequence with no cross-attention, and runs in just 8 denoising steps with no classifier-free guidance.

Before The Information's scoop, the AI community had openly speculated about HappyHorse's origin, with guesses including Alibaba's Wan 2.7 team, Alibaba Taotian's Future Life Lab led by Zhang Di, Kuaishou's Kling, and startup Sand.ai (founded by Swin Transformer co-authors Cao Yue and Zhang Zheng).

HappyHorse supports six prompt languages and native lip-sync across English, Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese, Korean, German and French, producing 5–8 second clips at 1080p — still short of Google Veo 3.1's 4K ceiling.

stories.headline: Ex-Rio Tinto CEO's Deep-Sea Mining Firm to Merge With Odyssey in $1B Critical Minerals Deal

key_facts.fact: American Ocean Minerals Corporation (AOMC), led by former Rio Tinto CEO Tom Albanese, announced a $1 billion all-stock merger with Odyssey Marine Exploration on April 8, aimed at building one of the world's largest portfolios of underwater mineral deposits

The combined company will absorb Odyssey's assets including its Cook Islands exploration license, plus those of CIC Limited (which Albanese chairs), and aims to extract polymetallic nodules containing cobalt, nickel, copper and manganese from the Pacific seabed

The deal includes $150 million in private placement from institutional and strategic investors plus $75 million in pre-public financing, with the combined company expected to have approximately $175 million in cash at closing

Roughly 30% of Odyssey's existing shareholders have entered voting support agreements, with the combined company to trade on Nasdaq under ticker 'AOMC' after expected close by August; Odyssey shares jumped 88% to $1.57 on Wednesday

Mike Rowe, the Emmy-award winning host of 'Dirty Jobs,' is a major investor and special advisor; AOM has asked the US government for two international licenses in the Pacific's Clarion-Clipperton Zone, putting it at odds with the International Seabed Authority

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Managed Agents, a Cloud Runtime for Building AI Agents at Scale

key_facts.fact: Anthropic on April 8, 2026 launched Claude Managed Agents in public beta, a composable API suite and fully managed runtime environment that handles sandboxing, credentials, state and tool execution so developers no longer have to build agent infrastructure themselves.

Anthropic says Managed Agents cuts the time to build and deploy a production-ready agent by roughly 10x and that on structured file-generation tasks it improved success rates by up to 10 percentage points over standard prompting.

Pricing separates model and runtime: model tokens are billed at standard API rates, plus $0.08 per hour of active agent work, with idle time not charged and web search billed separately at $10 per 1,000 queries.

Architecturally, Managed Agents splits each agent into three independently restartable components — the 'brain' (model and harness), the 'hands' (a sandbox with tools) and the 'session' (event log) — and keeps credentials for Git and MCP tools outside the sandbox so Claude cannot see them even on a successful prompt injection.

Early enterprise customers include Notion (Custom Agents in private alpha inside workspaces), Rakuten (agents rolled out in one week across product, sales, marketing, finance and HR via Slack and Teams), Asana (AI Teammates working inside project tasks), and Sentry (a Claude-powered debug partner for its Seer agent that writes patches and opens pull requests).

A research preview of the product lets individual agents spawn and direct other agents, enabling multi-agent coordination where a master agent delegates subtasks to specialized workers rather than running sequentially.

stories.headline: Arm CEO Rene Haas Set to Lead SoftBank International Business to Advance Project Izanagi AI Chip Strategy

key_facts.fact: Arm CEO Rene Haas is in line to lead much of SoftBank Group's international business while keeping his current role as head of Arm, according to a Financial Times report citing people familiar with the matter.

The new role would include oversight of operations in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and possibly robotics, designed to advance SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son's ambitions in semiconductors and AI.
The expanded responsibilities would enable Haas to advance Project Izanagi, SoftBank's AI chip strategy aimed at competing with established rivals such as Nvidia.
Haas was expected to take a title reflecting his senior role at SoftBank Group International, but was not expected to run the company's Vision Fund investment vehicles or its energy business.
The new role has not yet received approval from the boards of SoftBank and Arm, according to the Financial Times.

Last month Arm unveiled a new AI data centre chip that it said would add billions of dollars in revenue and mark a significant shift in strategy; its shares are up more than 10% since the announcement.

stories.headline: DC Circuit Refuses to Pause Pentagon's National Security Blacklisting of Anthropic

key_facts.fact: A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit on April 8, 2026 denied Anthropic's request to pause Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's supply-chain risk designation while its legal challenge plays out, in a win for the Trump administration.

The designation blocks Anthropic from Pentagon contracts and could trigger a government-wide blacklisting; Anthropic executives have said it could cost the company billions of dollars in lost business and reputational harm.

Hegseth designated Anthropic after it refused to allow the military to use Claude for U.S. surveillance or autonomous weapons; Anthropic says the move was illegal retaliation for its views on AI safety and violates its First Amendment rights.

The DC Circuit ruling contrasts with a March 26 decision by California federal judge Rita Lin, who blocked a parallel Hegseth order, calling the government's actions 'Orwellian,' 'arbitrary and capricious' and 'classic illegal First Amendment retaliation.'

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche called the DC Circuit stay 'a resounding victory for military readiness,' saying 'military authority and operational control belong to the Commander-in-Chief and Department of War, not a tech company,' while Anthropic said it remained confident the court will ultimately rule in its favor.
Anthropic's designation was the first time a U.S. company has been publicly labeled a supply-chain risk under procurement statutes previously reserved for companies connected to foreign adversaries.

organizations: U.S. Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit

stories.headline: Fed Minutes Show More Officials Open to Rate Hikes Amid Iran War Inflation Risk

key_facts.fact: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's March 17-18 meeting, released Wednesday, showed 'some' of the central bank's 19 policymakers supported changing post-meeting language to reflect the potential for a future rate hike — up from 'several' in January
'Many' Fed officials pointed to the risk that higher oil and gas prices stemming from the Iran war could keep inflation elevated for 'longer than expected, which could call for rate increases'
The Fed kept its key rate unchanged at about 3.6% at its March meeting, after cutting three times at the end of 2025; investors no longer expect a cut until late 2027 according to futures prices
Following the US-Iran ceasefire, market-implied probability of a Fed rate hike by year-end fell from 11.7% at the start of the week to just 0.8% by Wednesday morning, according to CME FedWatch
March US consumer-price index data due Friday is forecast to show a 0.9% monthly increase with year-over-year prices rising 3.4%, capturing initial impact of the gas price spike

stories.headline: Hologic Goes Private in $18.3B Blackstone-TPG Deal, Stock Delisted From Nasdaq

key_facts.fact: Hologic completed its take-private acquisition by Blackstone and TPG on Wednesday April 8, with the company's common stock ceasing to trade and being delisted from the Nasdaq Stock Market

The purchase price of $79 per share represented a 46% premium to Hologic's closing share price on May 23, 2025, with shareholders receiving $76 per share in cash plus a non-tradable contingent value right (CVR) worth up to $3 per share
The CVR is tied to Hologic's Breast Health business achieving specific global revenue milestones in fiscal 2026 and 2027

Following the transaction, Hologic appointed Jose (Joe) E. Almeida as chief executive officer effective immediately, succeeding Stephen MacMillan who retired after more than 12 years as chairman, president and CEO

stories.headline: India to Receive First Iranian Oil Cargo in 7 Years After US Waives Sanctions

key_facts.fact: India is set to receive its first oil from Iran in seven years, after the US temporarily removed sanctions on Iranian oil and refined products to ease supply shortages, according to ship tracking data from LSEG and Kpler

State-run Indian Oil Corporation purchased the cargo, currently aboard the Curacao-flagged very large crude carrier Jaya, which initially sailed toward China before changing course to India's east coast where it is set to arrive later this week
India, the world's third-biggest oil importer and consumer, has not received a cargo from Iran since May 2019 after US pressure forced refiners to stop buying Iranian crude
Kpler data shows Iranian crude oil on water near record-high levels above 180 million barrels in April, with another carrier 'Jordan' also signaling India as its discharge location
The waiver was a 30-day permission from US authorities aimed at stabilizing oil prices that had spiked after Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and may not be extended at the end of April

stories.headline: Iran Strikes UAE and Kuwait, Recloses Hormuz Hours After US Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Kuwait's army said its air defense units intercepted 28 drones launched from Iran in a 'dense wave' since 8:00 AM, with several aimed at oil facilities, power plants and desalination plants in the south, causing 'extensive material damage' to infrastructure
The UAE Ministry of Defense said it intercepted 17 Iranian missiles and 35 drones targeting the country since the ceasefire declaration
Iran reclosed the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday in response to Israeli attacks in Lebanon, less than 24 hours after agreeing to reopen the strategic waterway under the ceasefire deal

Iran's IRGC said it carried out the 99th wave of 'True Promise 4' operations, striking US bases including Jebel Ali port in the UAE and Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait, plus petrochemical facilities linked to ExxonMobil, Dow Chemical and Chevron Phillips in Saudi Arabia

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt called the closing of the Strait 'completely unacceptable,' while VP JD Vance described the truce as 'fragile' and said Iran 'thought that the ceasefire included Lebanon, and it just didn't'

Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said proceeding with peace talks would be 'unreasonable' because Washington had broken three of Tehran's 10 conditions, including Israeli attacks on Hezbollah and US refusal to accept Iranian uranium enrichment

stories.headline: Israel Strikes on Lebanon Kill 182 in Deadliest Day of Israel-Hezbollah War

key_facts.fact: Israeli strikes killed at least 182 people in Lebanon on Wednesday April 8, the highest single-day death toll in the Israel-Hezbollah war, with another 890 people injured according to Lebanon's health ministry

The strikes hit commercial and residential areas in Beirut, including central Beirut without warning, with the IDF issuing multiple evacuation warnings for Tyre and all residents of Beirut's southern suburbs
The Israeli offensive in Lebanon has killed at least 1,500 people and displaced 1.2 million others since Hezbollah was drawn into the conflict

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the strikes in unusually strong language, saying he was 'deeply alarmed by the mounting toll on civilians' and that the attacks pose 'a grave risk to the ceasefire'

Netanyahu and Trump said the US-Iran ceasefire did not cover Lebanon, while Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi insisted ending the Lebanon war was part of the agreement and Pakistan's PM said the truce applied 'everywhere including Lebanon'

stories.headline: Meta Commits Additional $21B to CoreWeave for AI Cloud Infrastructure Through 2032

key_facts.fact: Meta on April 9, 2026 announced an additional $21 billion commitment to AI cloud provider CoreWeave that runs from 2027 to 2032, on top of a prior $14.2 billion arrangement disclosed in September 2025 that runs through 2031.

CoreWeave data centers house hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GPUs used by hyperscalers; CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said Meta buying its own compute while also renting from CoreWeave reflects that 'there's just too much risk not to.'

Meta told investors it plans to spend between $115 billion and $135 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, nearly twice its 2025 capex, as it builds out AI infrastructure and added a separate $10 billion Texas data center in March.

The new Meta deal helps CoreWeave diversify away from Microsoft, which accounted for 62% of its 2024 revenue; after the contract no single customer will represent more than 35% of CoreWeave's total sales.

CoreWeave carried $21 billion in debt at the end of 2025 and borrowed another $8.5 billion in March to add infrastructure for new contracts; its stock is up 24% year to date while Meta is down about 7%.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Muse Spark, First Model From Superintelligence Labs Under Alexandr Wang

key_facts.fact: Meta debuted Muse Spark on April 8, 2026, calling it a natively multimodal reasoning model with tool-use, visual chain of thought, and multi-agent orchestration, and the first release from Meta Superintelligence Labs after a nine-month ground-up rebuild of its AI stack.

Muse Spark scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking 4th behind Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, and Claude Opus 4.6, after Meta gave Artificial Analysis early access for independent benchmarking.

In a so-called Contemplating mode that runs multiple agents reasoning in parallel, Muse Spark scores 58% on Humanity's Last Exam and 38% on FrontierScience Research, closing the gap with Gemini Deep Think and GPT Pro.
Meta built Muse Spark's health reasoning with input from more than 1,000 physicians and says it tops HealthBench Hard, beating GPT-5.4 by more than 2 points; Meta's stock rose 6.5% on the news.

Unlike prior Llama models, Muse Spark is closed-weight at launch — available in meta.ai and the Meta AI app, with a private API preview for select partners and paid broader API access promised later; Meta said it hopes to open-source future versions.
On agentic and coding benchmarks Muse Spark lags the leaders: it scored 42.5 on ARC-AGI-2 versus Gemini 3.1 Pro's 76.5, and 59.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 versus GPT-5.4's 75.1.

stories.headline: North Korea Fires Ballistic Missiles for Second Straight Day Toward East Sea

key_facts.fact: North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan toward the East Sea on Wednesday April 8 around 8:50 a.m. local time, the second launch event in two days
Japan issued an emergency alert and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi activated the country's national emergency response protocols, with the Japanese Coast Guard warning ships in adjacent waters
South Korea's National Security Office held an emergency security meeting with the Ministry of National Defense and Joint Chiefs of Staff, and reported the launches to President Lee Jae-myung

The launches followed a separate launch detected the day before, with experts saying they may be part of ongoing weapons development linked to solid-fuel missile technology for faster, more survivable nuclear delivery systems

The back-to-back launches came hours after South Korean President Lee Jae-myung expressed regret over drone flights by individuals into North Korea, with Kim Yo-jong calling Lee 'frank and broad-minded' but warning Seoul to 'stop any reckless provocation'

organizations: South Korea Joint Chiefs of Staff

stories.headline: OpenAI Foundation to Deploy $100M+ in Grants for AI-Driven Alzheimer's Research

key_facts.fact: The OpenAI Foundation announced on April 8, 2026 that it is working to finalize more than $100 million in grants this month across six research institutions to accelerate Alzheimer's research — generating new data, helping design new drugs, and expanding possible paths to treatment.

The Foundation framed Alzheimer's as one of four historical 'big killers' (heart disease, infectious disease, cancer, and neurodegenerative disease) and argued the disease's interacting genetic, protein-folding, inflammatory and synaptic causes make it a good fit for AI-driven discovery.

Alzheimer's Association president Joanne Pike said the initiative 'represents more than scientific progress — it's hope for millions of people, families, and anyone concerned about brain health,' and that the foundation expects to make further Alzheimer's grants throughout 2026 and beyond.

Gizmodo noted that OpenAI's 'AI for Alzheimer's' framing is notably more concrete than some peers: the Foundation attached specific dollar figures and credited human scientists, in contrast with the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub's broader 'cure or prevent all disease' pitch that has sometimes declined to disclose financial terms for acquisitions like EvolutionaryScale.

OpenAI safety researcher Wojciech Zaremba said the Foundation is taking 'an end-to-end approach to tackling Alzheimer's with AI,' supporting work 'from early diagnosis and better understanding of the disease, to accelerating' drug discovery.

stories.headline: OpenAI Pauses Stargate UK Data Center Project, Citing Energy Costs and Regulation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on April 9, 2026 that it is pausing its Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure project in the UK, citing the country's high energy costs and regulatory environment as it reins in ambitious spending plans.

The Stargate UK partnership was announced in September 2025 with Nvidia and UK data center operator Nscale; it was meant to explore offtake of up to 8,000 Nvidia GPUs in Q1 2026 at Cobalt Park in Tyneside, with potential to scale to 31,000 GPUs over time for 'sovereign compute' use cases in finance, research, and national security.

The first-quarter 2026 milestone to install roughly 8,000 Nvidia AI processors at Cobalt Park in Tyneside passed with no ground broken and OpenAI declining to give a revised timetable, according to earlier UK reporting.

Nscale — valued at $15 billion and with former UK deputy PM Nick Clegg on its board — has also delayed a separate project in Loughton, Essex, and analysis from Sightline Climate cited in UK reporting found up to 50% of large-scale data center projects worldwide are behind schedule, held up by energy constraints and supply-chain issues.

The pause marks a setback for UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's strategy of placing AI at the centre of Britain's growth push; OpenAI had appointed former Conservative chancellor George Osborne as managing director for countries in December 2025 to lead the international expansion of Stargate.

stories.headline: U.S. Air Forces Central Orders $9M+ in Skydio Autonomous Dock Drones to Secure Middle East Airbases

key_facts.fact: Skydio announced an order exceeding $9 million from U.S. Air Forces Central (USAFCENT) for Skydio Dock and X10 systems to secure U.S. airbases across the Middle East — one of the largest autonomous drone infrastructure deployments for international base security by the U.S. Air Force.

Skydio Docks deployed at strategic positions across airbases enable fully remote operation, launching X10 drones in under 20 seconds to patrol, verify, and respond to security threats, with a single operator able to manage multiple drones simultaneously.
When integrated sensors detect a threat, Skydio drones launch immediately and stream live high-definition and thermal video to the Base Defense Operations Center until the incident is resolved.

The X10D is the most widely deployed Group 1 Unmanned Aircraft System for USAF Security Forces and is the small UAS of choice for Air Combat Command Tactical Air Control Party Specialists and PACAF Security Forces.
Skydio is trusted by every branch of the U.S. military and the armed forces of 29 allied nations, with all drones and docking systems produced at its facility in Hayward, California.
The contract follows a $52 million U.S. Army order in March 2026 for over 2,500 Skydio X10D drones — the largest single-manufacturer small UAS purchase in Army history.

stories.headline: TSMC's CoWoS Advanced Packaging Grows at 80% CAGR as Nvidia Reserves Most Capacity

key_facts.fact: TSMC's most advanced chip packaging method currently in use, Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS), is growing at an 80% compound annual growth rate, according to the company's North America packaging head Paul Rousseau.
Nvidia has reserved a majority of the most advanced packaging capacity available at TSMC, which is the volume leader in advanced packaging.
TSMC is building its first U.S. advanced packaging facilities in Arizona this year and is ramping up two new packaging sites in Taiwan.

Almost all advanced packaging — the chip-making step that connects multiple small chips into a final GPU — currently happens in Asia, forcing chips manufactured in the U.S. to be shipped to Taiwan for packaging before returning.

Intel is technologically on par with TSMC on packaging and counts Amazon and Cisco as customers; on April 7, Elon Musk also tapped Intel to package custom chips for SpaceX, xAI and Tesla at the planned Terafab plant in Texas.

Georgetown CSET researcher John VerWey warned advanced packaging 'can emerge as a bottleneck very quickly' if companies don't make proactive capex investments to handle the surge in fab output coming in the next couple of years.

stories.headline: China's UniX AI Begins Global Deliveries of Panther Wheeled-Dual-Arm Humanoid Robot for Households

key_facts.fact: Suzhou-based UniX AI unveiled Panther, its third-generation full-size wheeled dual-arm humanoid robot, and commenced global deliveries, marking what it called a major milestone in bringing service humanoid robots into real homes.

Panther is fitted with what UniX AI calls the world's first mass-produced 8-degrees-of-freedom bionic arms, an adaptive intelligent gripper, and an omnidirectional four-wheel steering and four-wheel drive (4WS+4WD) chassis.

Panther features 34 high-DoF joints, an 80 cm vertical lift of the upper body to enable ground-level operation, and is built on a 48V power platform to deliver more output and stability for high-speed control.
Panther stands 1600-1750mm tall, has dual-arm load capacity of 12 kg, single-arm reach of 982 mm, repeatability of ±0.5 mm, and a four-wheel drive chassis with a movement speed of 2 m/s.

UniX AI deliberately chose a wheeled dual-arm architecture over the dominant legged-locomotion approach used by competitors, prioritizing 'usability, real-world applications, and customer experience' for commercial environments and complex indoor service scenarios.
